_meta.source: FF-SCORING-RULES.md Section 1, cross-checked 2026-09-13 against MFL TYPE=rules and TYPE=allRules exports
_meta.cross_check_result: Zero point-value disagreements found between Section 1 and the live MFL export. All 42 rule entries in the export matched an existing Section 1 line item exactly, and every Section 1 line item is represented in the export. See chat report for the one documentation-completeness issue found (the 'two unconfirmed values' the doc's header refers to are not actually marked anywhere in the body).
_meta.sleeper_field_note: sleeper_field_confidence is 'confirmed' only where the field name is unambiguous by content and naming. 'high' means it relies on Sleeper's idp_ prefix convention for individual-defender stats (reasonable, not independently confirmed by Sleeper docs). 'low' or 'unscorable' means a real, reported gap -- see notes. Verified against a full pull of all 18 weeks of real 2025 Sleeper stats data, not assumed from memory.
_meta.reverify: Re-pull TYPE=rules at the start of each season -- MFL leagues can change settings year to year.

rules.note: Sleeper only exposes FG-made COUNTS banded 0-19/20-29/30-39/40-49/50-59/60+, not exact yardage per kick, and its bands do not split at the league's exact 30-yard cutoff (a 30-yard FG falls in Sleeper's 30-39 band along with 31-39 yarders, which score under a different rule here). Approximating a 30-yard kick as if it were in the flat-3 band undercounts a real 31-39 yard kick and vice versa. Flagged in FF-SCORING-RULES.md itself as a known limitation -- label kicker output as approximate.

Same banding mismatch as the 0-30 rule. 'fgm_yds_over_30' exists and looks purpose-built for exactly this rule (total yards of made FGs over 30) but is unconfirmed -- worth checking directly against a real box score before trusting it for scoring.

Four candidate fields exist. Using idp_ff on the idp_-prefix convention (Sleeper's marker for the individual-defender version of a stat, consistent across tkl/tkl_ast/sack/int/pass_def/safe/fum_rec). Not independently confirmed against a real box score -- if a known forced-fumble game doesn't show up, check ff/st_ff/def_st_ff instead.
Same idp_ vs generic duplicate pattern as forced fumble.

'idp_def_td' removed from candidates 2026-09-13 -- it is now exclusively assigned to Interception return TD (#IR) below, guarded by scoring.py's DuplicateFieldMapping check so it can never be double-mapped here too. 'fum_rec_td' exists but its position eligibility (offense vs defense) is unconfirmed. Still unscored.

No matching field found anywhere in a full season of real Sleeper stats data (a team recovering its own fumble in the end zone is a rare event; Sleeper may not track it as a distinct category at all).
Same idp_ vs generic duplicate pattern.
No matching field found. Same rarity issue as offensive fumble recovery TD.

MFL's own glossary confirms TK = solo tackles specifically (distinct from AS = assists), matching Section 1's emphasis that solo/assist must not be combined. idp_tkl_solo chosen over plain tkl_solo on the idp_ convention.

MFL settings display as '1.5 per .5' because sacks record in half-sack increments; Zac confirmed this resolves to 3 per full sack. idp_sack is Sleeper's decimal sack count -- multiply directly by 3, do not round.

RESOLVED 2026-09-13, deliberate judgment call: 'idp_def_td' is a combined bucket that may also include defensive fumble-recovery TDs and blocked-kick-return TDs -- it is NOT confirmed to be interception-return-TDs exclusively. Assigned here rather than left unscored because (a) interception-return TDs are the most common of the flat-6 defensive-TD subtypes in a real season, so this is the best single home for the field, and (b) MFL pays exactly 6 points for every one of #DR/#IR/#BF/#MF/#BP regardless of subtype, so a point-total that lands here instead of on the true subtype is not a scoring error, only a mislabeled breakdown line. 'idp_def_td' is exclusively claimed by this rule -- #DR, #BF, and #MF below must never also reference it; scoring.py's load_rules() raises DuplicateFieldMapping if that ever happens. 'pass_int_td' remains wrong (it's the throwing QB's stat, not the defender's).

Sleeper has exactly one 'blocked a kick' field for the blocking player -- it does not distinguish FG (3pts) vs punt (3pts, same value here so low-risk) vs extra point (1pt, DIFFERENT value -- real risk). Using this field for BLF/BLP without a kick-type split will misattribute any blocked-XP as a blocked-FG-or-punt value (3 instead of 1) or vice versa. Flagging, not resolving.

'idp_def_td' removed from candidates 2026-09-13 -- exclusively assigned to Interception return TD (#IR), guarded against reuse here. 'blk_kick_ret_td' doesn't distinguish a blocked-FG-return from a blocked-punt-return TD. Left unscored -- per instruction, all blocked-kick rules stay unscored.
Same non-split issue as the TD count version.
Same combined block field as Blocked field goal -- see that note.

'idp_def_td' removed from candidates 2026-09-13 -- exclusively assigned to Interception return TD (#IR). 'blk_pr_td' looks like it could specifically mean 'blocked-punt return TD' by name, which would be a clean, confirmed-by-naming match unlike the FG-block-TD case -- worth a direct box-score check before trusting. Left unscored -- per instruction, all blocked-kick rules stay unscored.

'xp_blkd' looks like it is credited to the KICKING team/kicker (their XP got blocked), not the blocking defender. No confirmed field for the blocker's credit specific to an XP block, distinct from the combined FG/punt block field. This is the highest-risk gap in the whole file: if idp_blk_kick is used for BLE it will pay 1 point using a field that's actually shared with BLF/BLP's 3-point value, or vice versa -- guessing wrong here silently misscores by a factor of 3.
'idp_def_td' removed from candidates 2026-09-13 -- exclusively assigned to Interception return TD (#IR). No other candidate found. Left unscored.
